reforms.description: The establishment of the Economic Council of Canada was aimed at assessing medium- and long-term economic prospects and recommending policies to realize growth potential.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By providing informed recommendations on economic policies, the council aims to enhance the effectiveness of government interventions for growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The establishment of a new Department of Industry and the Economic Council of Canada.
reforms.importance_rationale: The creation of the Economic Council represents a significant institutional reform aimed at improving economic policy formulation.
reforms.source_quote: Other measures taken in 1963 consisted of the establishment of a new Department of Industry and the Economic Council of Canada.

reforms.description: The Canadian government introduced generous capital cost allowances for manufacturing or processing companies purchasing new machinery and equipment, along with a three-year tax exemption for those establishing new facilities in designated areas of slow growth and high unemployment, aimed at stimulating domestic expansion.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: These incentives are designed to stimulate investment in new machinery and facilities, which can enhance productivity and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The reforms have been put into effect as part of the government's strategy to boost manufacturing.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reforms provide significant but targeted incentives to stimulate investment in manufacturing, which is important for economic development.
reforms.source_quote: Similar incentives, together with a three-year tax exemption, for manufacturing and processing companies establishing new facilities in designated areas of slow growth and high unemployment.
